In many lands there is still expressed the beautiful sentiment that the gates of heaven stand wide open on Christmas Eve, and that he whose soul takes flight during its hallowed hours arrives straightway at the throne of grace.

37189-the-return-of-the-soldier.title: Of The Soldier
37189-the-return-of-the-soldier.creator: Rebecca West
37189-the-return-of-the-soldier.description: A book by Rebecca West. st lavish day of spring, and the sunlight was pouring through the tall, arched windows and the flowered curtains so brightly that in the old days a fat fist would certainly have been raised to point out the new, translucent glories of the rosebud. Sunlight was lying in great pools on the blue cork floor and the soft rugs, patterned with strange beasts, and threw dancing beams, which should have been gravely watched for hours, on the white paint and the blue distempered walls.

arxiv-1509-04737.title: Continuous generation of Rubidium vapor in hollow-core photonic band-gap fibers
arxiv-1509-04737.creator: Prathamesh S. Donvalkar, Sven Ramelow, Stéphane Clemmen, Alexander L. Gaeta
arxiv-1509-04737.description: Abstract We demonstrate high optical depths (50 ± {\pm} 5), lasting for hours in Rubidium-filled hollow-core photonic band-gap fibers, which represents a 1000X improvement over operation times previously reported. We investigate the vapor generation mechanism using both a continuous-wave and a pulsed light source and find that the mechanism for generating the Rubidium atoms is primarily due to thermal vaporization.

arxiv-2211-09748.title: Probing for Incremental Parse States in Autoregressive Language Models
arxiv-2211-09748.creator: Tiwalayo Eisape, Vineet Gangireddy, Roger P. Levy, Yoon Kim
arxiv-2211-09748.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tiwalayo Eisape, Vineet Gangireddy, Roger P. Levy, Yoon Kim. Next-word predictions from autoregressive neural language models show remarkable sensitivity to syntax. This work evaluates the extent to which this behavior arises as a result of a learned ability to maintain implicit representations of incremental syntactic structures. We extend work in syntactic probing to the incremental setting and present several probes for extracting incomplete syntactic structure (operationalized through parse states from a stack-based parser) from autoregressive language models.

arxiv-2304-14378.title: Functional Diffusion Maps
arxiv-2304-14378.creator: M. Barroso, C.M. Alaíz, J.L. Torrecilla, A. Fernández
arxiv-2304-14378.description: Abstract Nowadays many real-world datasets can be considered as functional, in the sense that the processes which generate them are continuous. A fundamental property of this type of data is that in theory they belong to an infinite-dimensional space. Although in practice we usually receive finite observations, they are still high-dimensional and hence dimensionality reduction methods are crucial.

arxiv-2406-17433.title: Mind the Graph When Balancing Data for Fairness or Robustness
arxiv-2406-17433.creator: Jessica Schrouff, Alexis Bellot, Amal Rannen-Triki, Alan Malek, Isabela Albuquerque, Arthur Gretton, Alexander D’Amour, Silvia Chiappa
arxiv-2406-17433.description: Abstract Failures of fairness or robustness in machine learning predictive settings can be due to undesired dependencies between covariates, outcomes and auxiliary factors of variation. A common strategy to mitigate these failures is data balancing, which attempts to remove those undesired dependencies.

arxiv-2410-01097.title: On the number of solutions of decomposable form inequalities
arxiv-2410-01097.creator: C.L. Stewart
arxiv-2410-01097.description: Abstract . In 2001 Thunder gave an estimate for the number of integer solutions of decomposable form inequalities under the assumption that the forms are of finite type. The purpose of this article is to generalize this result to forms which are of essentially finite type.

arxiv-2504-01147.title: The impact of glasma on heavy quark spectra and correlations
arxiv-2504-01147.creator: \firstname Dana \lastname Avramescu \fnsep, \firstname Vincenzo \lastname Greco \fnsep, \firstname Tuomas \lastname Lappi \fnsep, \firstname Heikki \lastname Mäntysaari \fnsep, \firstname David \lastname Müller \fnsep
arxiv-2504-01147.description: Abstract We investigate the effect of the glasma classical color fields, produced in the very early stage of heavy-ion collisions, on the transport of heavy quarks. The glasma fields evolve according to the classical Yang-Mills equations, while the dynamics of heavy quarks is described by Wong’s equations.

arxiv-2507-12359.title: Cluster Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
arxiv-2507-12359.creator: Nikolaos Giakoumoglou, Tania Stathaki
arxiv-2507-12359.description: Abstract We introduce Cluster Contrast (CueCo), a novel approach to unsupervised visual representation learning that effectively combines the strengths of contrastive learning and clustering methods. Inspired by recent advancements, CueCo is designed to simultaneously scatter and align feature representations within the feature space.

pmc-10539296.title: Computer aided progression detection model based on optimized deep LSTM ensemble model and the fusion of multivariate time series data
pmc-10539296.creator: Hager Saleh, Eslam Amer, Tamer Abuhmed, Amjad Ali, Ala Al-Fuqaha, Shaker El-Sappagh
pmc-10539296.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common form of dementia. Early and accurate detection of AD is crucial to plan for disease modifying therapies that could prevent or delay the conversion to sever stages of the disease. As a chronic disease, patient’s multivariate time series data including neuroimaging, genetics, cognitive scores, and neuropsychological battery provides a complete profile about patient’s status. This data has been used to build machine learning and deep learning (DL) models for the early detection of the disease.

pmc-11316322.title: The ethical dimension of personal health monitoring in the armed forces: a scoping review
pmc-11316322.creator: Dave Bovens, Eva van Baarle, Kirsten Ziesemer, Bert Molewijk
pmc-11316322.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPersonal Health Monitoring (PHM) has the potential to enhance soldier health outcomes. To promote morally responsible development, implementation, and use of PHM in the armed forces, it is important to be aware of the inherent ethical dimension of PHM.

pmc-11630776.title: Reclaiming the narrative: countering harmful commercial discourses
pmc-11630776.creator: May C I van Schalkwyk, Nason Maani, Benjamin Hawkins, Mark Petticrew, Kent Buse
pmc-11630776.description: The discourses promoted by powerful commercial actors whose business activities are damaging to health undermine the potential for the transformational changes urgently needed to address pressing public health and environmental threats globally. This piece provides an analysis of corporate discursive practices and the mechanisms through which they contaminate scientific and policy debates and harm public and environmental health.

pmc-12495655.creator: Likang Li, Lei Zhang, Yafei Chen, Fen Yang, Xiuxia Song, Hong Liang, Wei Yuan, Honglei Ji, Min Luan, Maohua Miao

pmc-12595876.title: Psychological distress and loneliness among European university students during the COVID-19 pandemic: a European survey
pmc-12595876.creator: Caixin Tian, Roberto Ariel Abeldaño Zuñiga, Moréniké Oluwátóyìn Foláyan, Jarno Tuominen, Jorma I. Virtanen
pmc-12595876.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic and various consequent isolation, quarantine and curfew measures to curb the spread of the virus caused an increase in anxiety, depression, and loneliness among university students. The aim of this study was to assess the association between psychological distress and loneliness among university students in Europe during the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-12618135.title: The Relationship Between Myocardial Fibrosis in Hypertensive Patients With Preserved Ejection Fraction and the Severity of Systemic Inflammatory Status Is Mediated by Epicardial Adipose Tissue: A Multicenter Cohort Study
pmc-12618135.creator: Wanting Wang, Runze Zhu, Wenxian Wang, Yan Gao, Jie Liu, Liang Wu, Ximing Wang
pmc-12618135.description: This study aims to investigate the impact of exacerbated systemic inflammatory status on the degree of myocardial fibrosis and strain impairment in hypertensive patients with preserved ejection fraction, as well as the role played by epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) in this process.

pmc-13167339.title: Perioperative hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and venous thromboembolism risk: a scoping review of available evidence and guidance
pmc-13167339.creator: Omar Helmy, Celine Iswarya Partha Sarathi, Diwakar Sarma
pmc-13167339.description: SummaryObjectiveHormone replacement therapy (HRT) is used to manage menopausal symptoms, but its perioperative use raises concerns about increased venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk. Clinical guidelines vary, with some advising temporary discontinuation before surgery. This scoping review aims to synthesise evidence and guidance on whether perioperative cessation of HRT influences postoperative VTE risk.

pmc-13562996.title: Determinants of generalized trust: Economic, Institutional, and personal factors
pmc-13562996.creator: Jorge Soria Ruiz-Ogarrio, Jorge Moya Velasco, Carlos Estevez Mendoza, Josep Navarro-Ortiz, Mahyudin Ahmad, Andreas Kyriacou, Mahyudin Ahmad, Josep Navarro-Ortiz, Albert Jiansong Zheng, Josep Navarro-Ortiz, Andreas Kyriacou, Josep Navarro-Ortiz
pmc-13562996.description: BackgroundGeneralised trust matters for social cohesion, economic exchange and institutional life, but there is still disagreement about the conditions under which it emerges. This article studies whether the same economic, institutional and personal factors are linked to three forms of trust, namely trust in most people, trust in people met for the first time and trust in neighbours.
